chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Adhina, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked one of the two (peace be upon them both) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'The cattle quadrupeds are permissible for you' [5:1]. So he said: The foetus in the belly of its mother, when it grows hair and fluff, then its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother — that is what God, Mighty and Majestic, meant.

key_terms.بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعَامِ: cattle quadrupeds (the livestock mentioned in Quran 5:1)
key_terms.ذَكَاةٌ: ritual slaughter (dhabh — the Islamic method of slaughtering)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the foetus found in the belly of a slaughtered animal according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim, a prominent disciple of the Imams, inquired about the Quranic verse permitting cattle (5:1). The Imam clarified that the phrase 'cattle quadrupeds' includes the foetus in the womb of a slaughtered animal: if the foetus has developed hair or fluff (indicating sufficient development), its slaughter is considered accomplished through the slaughter of its mother. This ruling established a key principle in Shia halal slaughter jurisprudence — the foetus does not require a separate ritual slaughter if its mother has been properly slaughtered.
word_analysis: one of the two of them
